column1:
Cautiously positive, but more muted after incorporating the July 2017 SLOOS. The FOMC text points to solid job gains, moderate growth, and an accommodative stance with a transparent, gradual balance sheet normalization, which supports confidence and reduces policy uncertainty. The Financial Stability Report adds prudence given elevated asset valuations and pockets of leverage, even as bank capital/liquidity remain solid.

SLOOS tilts the balance a bit more cautious: domestic banks reported weaker demand across key CRE segments (construction, land development, multifamily) and for consumer credit (auto and credit card), alongside tighter standards for consumer loans. Foreign banks reported tighter standards across C&I (for small, middle-market, and large firms) and CRE, despite some strengthening in CRE loan demand. Offsetting this somewhat, residential mortgage standards eased (including jumbo, QM, and GSE), which should modestly support housing, with some categories unchanged.

Netting these, credit appetite and availability look mixed-to-soft outside housing, arguing for patience and a data-dependent, gradual path. The tone remains mildly positive on growth and labor, but tempered further by softer loan demand and some tightening in standards.
